Because most of the country already has an ISP. ISP's are considered natural monopolies. Which implies that it is difficult for more than one to survive in a market at a time. A monopoly is necessary because ISP's have high fixed costs (laying cables), but extremely low marginal costs (cost that occur directly because of an increase in output, like adding a new customer.)

Before I go further it is important to know that in theory, in a COMPETETIVE market firm's operate where their marginal revenue (price) equals their marginal cost. So with that in mind if there was competition ISP's would have to charge a very low price to be competitive, or go out of business. But as stated earlier they have a high fixed cost. So firm's that try to gain entry to a market that already has a ISP will have an extremely hard time recouping their fixed costs.
